translation.english_text: (While Damayanti slept, in the middle of the night I deceived her, betrayed her, tore away half her sari and set off running! I went, I went, leaving that virtuous woman to suffer. He went—he went away altogether.)
(In the same way, Paranthaman follows Nala and goes away, leaving Bama to suffer. Bama is bewildered when she cannot find Paranthaman.)
Would the wickedness of abandoning one's beloved in the forest, in pitch darkness, be enough for kings?...
notes: The source supplies no speaker label for this closing line; none is invented. The Nala-Damayanti parallel is preserved without importing outside text.
